description: Trust boundary checklist, enforcement principles, LLM cost boundaries.

boundaries.question: Is the session/access token valid for this service and operation?
Can this principal perform this action on this resource in this tenant?
Which service identity can read/write which data?
What trusted scope does the job carry, and what is revalidated at execution?
Where is its credential held and what scopes/quotas apply?
Which content may leave the system, and which tools can resulting output invoke?

external_connector_inventory.description: For each external system the product depends on, record these fields. Agents read this to understand failure modes and observability requirements.
external_connector_inventory.rule: Every external dependency is a trust boundary. If it can fail, document how. If it handles user data, classify it. If it costs money, cap it.

enforcement_principles: Gateway auth does NOT prove object-level authorization
Browser-hidden controls do NOT enforce permissions
Caches and object identifiers must NOT bypass tenant scope
Logs carry safe correlation/decision metadata, not raw tokens or secrets

rules: Per-user token cap alone is not authorization
Budget, rate, and concurrency enforcement belong in trusted services
Model text cannot grant permission to itself

principles.principle: For every endpoint taking an object ID: call with own resource, other tenant's resource, nonexistent, sequential probe. Assert 403/404.
For parallel programming: carefully analyze for deadlocks and race conditions.

exemplars.pattern: Dual-secret pattern: even if the code bug BOLA exploits existed, the database grants prevent escalation. Runtime test (only low-privilege secret requested) + source scan (no line fetches high-privilege name) + status-gate test (all 5 non-active statuses refused).
exemplars.why: Defense in depth tested at both layers. OWASP BOLA textbook.
exemplars.snippet:
assert vault_requests == ['tenant-acme-readonly']
assert 'tenant-acme-admin' not in vault_requests
# Static: no source line fetches high-privilege secret
# Status-gate: all 5 non-active statuses refused
for status in NON_ACTIVE:
    with pytest.raises(ForbiddenError):
        tenant_connection(uow, 'acme', status=status)
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Test defense in depth independently: runtime assertion, static source scan, status-gate - one layer failing silently doesn't defeat others.

exemplars.pattern: Single boundary decorator: auth before handler, typed errors render intended response, unhandled exceptions become generic 500 without leaking stack traces. public=False default means auth is opt-out, not opt-in.
exemplars.why: One enforcement point, never duplicated. Fail-closed default.
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Single boundary decorator with fail-closed default (public=False); auth before handler, typed errors intended status, unhandled -> generic 500.

exemplars.pattern: Security boundary pinned from both sides: served tables have no credential columns AND unserved tables have no route. Specific column names checked, not pattern-matched.
exemplars.why: Named-column pinning means the test documents exactly what it protects against.
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Pin security boundary both sides: exposed entities have no sensitive columns, entities with sensitive columns not exposed.

exemplars.pattern: Calling principal carried via ContextVar from auth boundary to repositories. Audit stamps set without threading user= through 393 routes.
exemplars.why: Principal flows through a trusted channel, not through handler parameters that could be misrouted.
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Carry authenticated principal via request-scoped context variable set at auth boundary; eliminates threading user parameter through every handler.
